sections.title: Getting Started
sections.content:
Welcome to SOLIS (Singlet Oxygen Luminescence Investigation System)!

1. **Load Data**: Use File → Open Folder to select a directory containing your decay files
2. **Select Compounds**: Check the compounds you want to analyze in the Data Browser
3. **Run Analysis**: Choose Analysis → Homogeneous → Kinetics and QY
4. **View Results**: Results appear in the browser tabs (Kinetics, Statistics, Quantum Yield)
5. **Generate Plots**: Right-click compounds or results to create plots, or use the toolbar buttons (Individual Plots / Plot Merged)

sections.title: File Menu
sections.content:
**Open Folder**: Load data files from a directory

**Save Session**: Save your current work (data, results, plots, settings) to a .solis.json file

**Load Session**: Restore a previously saved session

**Export Results**: Export kinetics results and statistics to CSV files

**Reset Session**: Clear all data and start fresh

sections.title: Analysis Types
sections.content:
**Homogeneous Analysis**:
• Kinetics and QY: Analyze homogeneous decay kinetics and calculate quantum yields
• Linearity Check: Study variation of α with absorption or excitation intensity

**Heterogeneous (Vesicle) Analysis**:
• 3-exponential fit for heterogeneous systems with lipid/water compartments
• Grid search optimization for τ_Δ(water) and τ_Δ(lipid)

**Surplus Analysis**:
• 4-step method for heterogeneous systems
• Can run automatically after homogeneous analysis

sections.title: File Naming Convention
sections.content:
**Decay Files**:
Decay_[Compound]_EX[λ]nm_tauD[value]_QY[value]_QYsd[sd]_EI[value][unit].csv

Example:
Decay_TMPyP_EX400nm_tauD3.5_QY0.98_QYsd0.08.csv

**Absorption Files**:
Abs_[Compound].csv

Example:
Abs_TMPyP.csv

**Fluorescence Emission Files**:
FL_[Compound].csv

Example:
FL_TMPyP.csv

**Phosphorescence Emission Files**:
Ph_[Compound].csv

Example:
Ph_TMPyP.csv

**Notes**:
• [Compound] must match exactly across all file types for the same compound
• All spectral files (Abs, FL, Ph) use the same CSV format: first column is wavelength (nm), remaining columns are replicate intensities
• Multiple replicate columns are automatically averaged

sections.title: SNR Thresholds
sections.content:
Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) thresholds determine data quality:

• **Homogeneous**: Default 5:1 (moderate quality required)
• **Heterogeneous**: Default 50:1 (high quality required for 3-exponential fit)

You can adjust these in Preferences → SNR Thresholds.

SNR is always displayed as a ratio (e.g., 52.6:1), not in dB.

sections.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
sections.content:
**File Menu**:
• Ctrl+O: Open Folder
• Ctrl+S: Save Session
• Ctrl+Shift+O: Load Session
• Ctrl+E: Export Results
• Ctrl+R: Reset Session
• Ctrl+Q: Exit

**Analysis Menu**:
• Ctrl+H: Homogeneous Kinetics and QY
• Ctrl+L: Linearity Check
• Ctrl+V: Heterogeneous (Vesicle) Analysis

**Help**:
• F1: Open this help dialog

sections.title: Spectral Overlay Plots
sections.content:
SOLIS can plot and overlay absorption (Abs), fluorescence (FL), and phosphorescence (Ph) spectra.

**Standalone Plots**:
• Right-click any Abs, FL, or Ph compound in the browser → **Plot Spectrum** (or **Plot FL Spectrum** / **Plot Ph Spectrum**)
• Or select compounds and click the **Individual Plots** toolbar button
• Shows raw intensity vs. wavelength for that compound

**Overlay Plots** (normalized 0–1):
• Right-click an FL compound → **Plot Abs + FL Overlay** (requires a matching Abs file)
• Right-click a Ph compound → **Plot Abs + Ph Overlay** (requires a matching Abs file)
• All spectra are normalized to 0–1 on a common y-axis for shape comparison

**Merged Spectra** (multiple compounds):
• Select multiple FL or Ph compounds (Ctrl+Click), right-click → **Plot Merged FL/Ph Spectra**
• Or select compounds and click the **Plot Merged** toolbar button
• Overlays all selected spectra in different colors

**Mixed Spectrum Overlay** (different types):
• Select compounds from different sections (e.g., one Abs + one FL + one Ph) using Ctrl+Click
• Click the **Plot Merged** toolbar button
• A dialog asks for a reference wavelength — each spectrum is normalized to its nearest peak within ±100 nm of this value
• Colors: Abs = black, FL = green, Ph = purple (dashed)

**Export**:
• All spectral plots support CSV, PDF, SVG, and PNG export via right-click or the tab toolbar

sections.title: Plot Appearance
sections.content:
Customize the appearance of any plot for publication or presentation.

**Opening the Dialog**:
• View menu → Plot Appearance
• Or right-click any plot → Plot Appearance

**Font Controls**:
• **Family**: Choose from installed system fonts (e.g., Arial, Times New Roman, Helvetica)
• **Sizes**: Independently set font size for title, axis labels, tick labels, legend, and annotations
• **Weight**: Normal or bold, per element

**Grid**:
• Toggle grid on/off
• Style: solid, dashed, or dotted
• Opacity and color controls

**Line Widths**:
• Data points, fit curves, and residual markers each have independent width controls

**Colors**:
• Fit line color, alternative fit color, grid color

**Apply / Reset**:
• **Apply**: Changes are applied live to the selected plot
• **Reset**: Restores all settings to defaults

**Width Bar** (below each plot):
• Slider controls canvas width as a percentage of available space (10–100%)
• Snap points at 25%, 40%, 60%, 80% for quick sizing
• Far-right position = Auto (fills available space)
• DPI spinner (72–1200, default 300) controls export resolution
• The displayed size label shows the current percentage

**WYSIWYG Export**:
• What you see is what you get — the exported image matches the displayed canvas size and DPI setting

sections.title: Export Formats
sections.content:
Right-click any plot to access export options.

**PNG** (Portable Network Graphics):
• Raster format at the DPI set in the width bar (default 300)
• Good for presentations and documents
• File size depends on DPI and canvas dimensions

**SVG** (Scalable Vector Graphics):
• Vector format — infinitely scalable without quality loss
• Ideal for publications and further editing in Inkscape or Adobe Illustrator
• Text remains editable as vector paths

**PDF** (Portable Document Format):
• Vector format with embedded fonts
• Publication-ready, maintains quality at any zoom level

**CSV** (Comma-Separated Values):
• Exports the numerical data underlying the plot
• Includes time, intensity, fit curves, residuals, wavelength data, etc.
• Useful for re-plotting in other software or further analysis

**Controlling Dimensions**:
• Use the width bar slider to set canvas width (percentage of available space)
• Adjust DPI for raster exports (PNG)
• Vector exports (SVG, PDF) are resolution-independent

sections.title: About SOLIS
sections.content:
SOLIS — Singlet Oxygen Luminescence Investigation System

**Version**: 1.1.0
**License**: CC BY-NC 4.0 (Non-commercial)
**Language**: Python 3.10+ (PyQt6, matplotlib, NumPy, SciPy)

**Author**: Erick Leite Bastos
Instituto de Quimica, Universidade de Sao Paulo

**Features**:
• Homogeneous decay kinetics analysis
• Quantum yield calculations (A-based method)
• Heterogeneous (vesicle) analysis with grid search
• Surplus analysis for heterogeneous systems
• Linearity checks (Beer-Lambert, Excitation Intensity)
• Fluorescence and phosphorescence spectral analysis
• Mixed spectrum overlay with peak-based normalization
• Advanced spike detection and masking
• Session save/load with full state preservation
• Plot appearance customization (fonts, grid, colors, line widths)
• WYSIWYG export with adjustable width and DPI
• SVG, PNG, PDF, and CSV export
• Publication-quality matplotlib plots

**GitHub**: https://github.com/el-bastos/SOLIS
**Zenodo**: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18475839
